title: Pin resilience contracts and deprecation signal flow
creator: Elena Park
description: Deliver a clear, testable contract for fallback behavior when a customer pins to a specific model version, and implement a machine-friendly deprecation signal flow so we can safely migrate pinned workloads without silent regressions. This ticket covers policy language, routing decisions, signal propagation (API headers/metrics), and the first-pass enforcement in the runtime and router.
background: Customers can pin to exact model versions for deterministic behavior. When a pinned model becomes unavailable, degraded, or is scheduled for deprecation, the platform must follow a predictable, observable fallback policy. Current fallback behavior is fragmented: some routes try region fallback, others immediately fail to a less-capable variant. There is no uniform deprecation signal and no published contract that the router/runtime can rely on. This causes customer incidents and surprises during model rollouts.
proposal_summary: Define a pin-resilience contract that: (1) enumerates fallback tiers and deterministic ordering, (2) specifies SLO/quality thresholds that must be met for a fallback to be considered, (3) defines deprecation signaling (metadata + TTL) and an API surface to communicate fallback decisions to end-users, and (4) implements telemetry to measure correctness and customer exposure. Implement initial enforcement via the routing layer with feature flags to rollback quickly.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable 'pin-resilience' contract published in our onboarding docs describing fallback tier order and evaluation rules

Routing layer implements fallback ordering: regional-equivalent -> model-variant with compatibility contract -> quantized-compatible variant -> client-visible hard-fail only when no acceptable fallback is available
Deprecation signal format written and emitted by model onboarding service (model metadata: deprecated: true, deprecation_date, replacement_candidates list, deprecation_reason, grace_period_days)
Router attaches headers on proxied responses: 'x-rw-fallback-reason' and 'x-rw-served-model' when fallback is used
Automated alerts when >0.5% of pinned requests trigger fallback for a customer over a 10m window
End-to-end e2e tests covering each fallback tier and deprecation-triggered rerouting
No silent quality regressions: fallback candidates must pass a lightweight compatibility test (embedding similarity threshold or small eval) before being served to a pinned customer
Feature flag gates exist allowing safe rollback of fallback enforcement per region and per release
design_decisions: Fallback tiers are ordered and deterministic. We will not attempt multi-hop exploration (no probabilistic candidate trials) during the initial rollout to avoid user-visible flakiness.

Quality gating is required: fallback candidate must meet a pre-defined delta on the customer's pinned model performance profile (default: <= 3% drop in key eval metric or <= 5% drop in embedding similarity).
Region affinity: prefer same-region capacity first even if a slightly lower-quality variant exists in the pinned region; network latency wins when p95 delta would exceed 50ms.

Deprecation metadata is authoritative. Onboarding service will mark versions deprecated and provide replacement candidates; router trusts the metadata and will start additional safeguards when deprecation_date approaches.
Expose fallback reasons and served-model in response headers to help customers and SDKs understand behavior and allow client-side tracking.

We will avoid changing customer-visible defaults for the hosted API; pinned customers will opt-in to automatic fallbacks via a new 'pin_fallback_policy' in their project configuration. Default policy is 'automatic-with-gates'.
Security: deprecation and fallback signals include no PII and are safe to emit in headers; sensitive internal reasons remain in private logs only.
fallback_policy_contract: Tier 0 - Exact: Serve pinned version if healthy and capacity available.
Tier 1 - Regional-equivalent: Route to the same model+version in another shard/zone/availability region, if latency penalty < 50ms p95 and instance health == healthy.

Tier 2 - Verified-variant: Serve a model variant that declares compatibility (same tokenizer, same output schema) and passes a lightweight compatibility test and perf thresholds (latency and key eval metric deltas within contract).

Tier 3 - Quantized/optimized-variant: Serve a lower-precision or quantized build of the pinned model only when the quality delta is within contract and it reduces latency/cost significantly, and if customer policy allows quantized fallbacks.
Tier 4 - Degraded fallback / best-effort: As last resort, serve an older major version marked as acceptable by customer during pin creation or explicitly included in replacement_candidates metadata.
Hard-fail: If no candidate meets contract, surface a 409 'PinnedModelUnavailable' with structured body explaining required actions and include 'x-rw-fallback-reason: none_acceptable'.
deprecation_signal_flow: Model owner tags version as deprecated in onboarding service GUI or API with fields: deprecated=true, deprecation_date=YYYY-MM-DD, grace_period_days=N, replacement_candidates=[ids], deprecation_note=string.
Onboarding service publishes change to model-catalog stream; catalog consumers (router, console, optimize) pick up the change within 30s.

When deprecation_date <= now + grace_period_days, router begins conservative routing: prefer replacement candidates when pinned customers have 'auto_migrate' enabled; otherwise keep serving exact version and mark in console warnings.
7/3/1 day pre-deprecation warnings emitted to project owners and in-console banners; warnings include compatibility checklist and links to migration playbook.
If deprecated version becomes unhealthy during grace window, router follows fallback contract but marks events as 'deprecation-triggered' for telemetry and escalation.

After deprecation_date + grace_period_days, if customer has not migrated and pin is still present: depending on customer's pin policy, either auto-migrate to best candidate (if allowed) or place the pinned project into 'manual-migration-required' state and begin SLA-level communications.
routing_and_compatibility_checks: Router will implement a two-phase check for candidates: health-check + lightweight compatibility test (100-sample prompt bank run or embedding similarity quick-check depending on workload).
Compatibility thresholds are parameterized per model family and published in the model catalog performance profile (example fields: eval_metric_name, baseline_score, acceptable_delta_pct).

When routing across regions, router computes an estimated end-to-end p95 impact combining network delta and candidate latency. If estimated p95 > pinned p95 + 50ms, candidate is rejected unless customer policy allows higher latency.
A scoped cache of recent compatibility test results is maintained to avoid repeated evaluation; results expire in 10 minutes or when model/variant updates occur.
When fallback involves a model variant with different tokens-per-second characteristics, router adjusts batching windows to preserve latency SLOs and reports cost delta to console.
Router will attach structured reason codes in internal logs (example: FALLBACK_TIER_2_COMPATIBLE, FALLBACK_TIER_1_REGION, NO_ACCEPTABLE_CANDIDATE) to ease analysis.
telemetry_and_metrics: Per-project metric: pinned_fallback_rate (count and ratio) with tags: project_id, pinned_model_id, fallback_tier, region, reason_code
Alert rule: pinned_fallback_rate > 0.5% over 10m (P1) and > 5% over 30m (Critical)
Histogram: fallback_latency_penalty_ms comparing pinned baseline vs served candidate p95
Audit events: deprecation_published, deprecation_warning_sent, deprecation_auto_migrate_triggered, pin_unavailable_email_sent
Expose user-facing logs via Console with links to request traces and the 'served-model' header for debugging
Daily report in console 'Pin Resilience' dashboard summarizing customers affected and top models by fallback volume
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish proposal and contract doc, gather engineering + product + support signoff
Week 1: Implement deprecation metadata propagation and router header wiring behind feature flag 'pin_resilience_v1'
Week 2: Implement lightweight compatibility checks and candidate evaluation libraries; add unit/e2e tests
Week 3: Canary rollout to non-production orgs and internal teams (10 orgs). Monitor pinned_fallback_rate and errors
Week 4: Gradual ramp to 10% of hosted production traffic for orgs with <10% p99 SLA risk; observe for 72h
Week 5: If stable, enable for all hosted projects with default 'automatic-with-gates' policy; provide opt-out via project settings
Rollback plan: feature-flag disable at router or global kill-switch in control-plane, page on >1% customer-visible regressions or rising incident rate
Communication: Email + Console banners to pinned customers explaining new fallback headers and migration recommendations
test_plan: Unit tests for routing decision engine covering each fallback tier and rejection paths
Integration tests with a mocked onboarding catalog including deprecation events and replacement_candidates
E2E tests using a synthetic workload that asserts p95 latency guarantees and that headers are present when fallback occurs
Load test to ensure compatibility checks scale (compat-check DB cache hit behavior and worker autoscaling)
Chaos scenarios: kill exact-version hosts to ensure deterministic fallbacks and no routing loops
Post-deploy canary checks validating pinned_fallback_rate and compatibility-test pass rate before wider rollout
migration_steps: Publish user-facing docs describing pin_fallback_policy settings and example usage
Add console UI to show pinned projects and recommended replacement candidates with 'one-click' preview migration
Provide SDK hooks so customers can opt into different policies and surface headers in their app logs
Run a migration pilot with two large customers (marketing + billing) to validate replacement_candidates metadata and acceptance criteria
Backfill catalog compatibility metadata for top 50 models by traffic before full rollout
open_questions: Should we allow probabilistic multi-candidate trialing for a small percentage of requests to learn which candidate gives best empirical quality? (Pros: data; Cons: flakiness)
What default acceptable_delta_pct should be used per model family? Product wants 5%, research suggests 3% for LLM quality-sensitive tasks.
How do enterprise contracts affect auto-migrate behavior? Some customers may require manual signoff before migration.
Do we expose deprecation reasons in public console or keep them internal? (We propose limited public reason text with escalation links.)
How to handle custom fine-tuned models where replacement_candidates are likely absent? We need a manual migration playbook.
